links.outcome: Accuracy of VLM answers after deferring/excluding high-semantic-entropy questions
links.effect: Filtering DSE > 0.3 raised accuracy from 51.7% to 76.3% for GPT-4o (334/706 retained) and 54.8% to 63.8% for GPT-4.1 (499/706 retained), both p < 0.001.
links.quote: After filtering out high-entropy questions (DSE > 0.3), accuracy on the remaining questions was 76.3% (retained questions: 334/706) for GPT-4o and 63.8% (retained questions: 499/706) for GPT-4.1 (both p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Uncertainty-based filtering of hallucination-prone questions improving answer accuracy
links.effect: DSE filtering at a 0.3 threshold increased GPT-4o accuracy from 51.7% to 76.3% and GPT-4.1 from 54.8% to 63.8%, while answering fewer questions.
links.quote: DSE filtering at a 0.3 threshold increased GPT-4o accuracy from 51.7% to 76.3% and GPT-4.1 from 54.8% to 63.8%, while answering fewer questions.

unlisted_practices: Discrete semantic entropy (sampling-based consistency) filtering to reject hallucination-prone questions in black-box VLMs

screen.reason: Evaluates discrete semantic entropy as an output filtering / rejection safeguard on existing commercial VLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1) to suppress hallucinations and improve accuracy in radiology visual question answering.
